passage:
To: Pranav
Subject: Blocked exit and loose cable, kitchen
Hi Pranav,
I am writing about two things I saw in the staff kitchen at four today. First, four boxes of tins are stacked in front of the back fire exit, so the door cannot open fully. Second, the toaster's cable has a split in the plastic near the plug. I have moved my own things away from the socket and put a note on the toaster. Could the boxes be moved to the store room, and the toaster replaced, before Friday's team lunch? I can help carry the boxes tomorrow at nine. Thank you, Jahnavi

Reply from Pranav: Thanks, Jahnavi. Boxes moved, toaster removed. Good catch.

qa.q: How many boxes were stacked in front of the back fire exit?
qa.a: Four boxes of tins were stacked in front of the back fire exit.

qa.q: Why does Jahnavi offer to help carry the boxes?
qa.a: Jahnavi is concerned about the blocked exit and the split cable and eager to see them fixed before Friday's lunch, so Jahnavi offers help to turn the report into action.

qa.q: What made Jahnavi's report easy to act on?
qa.a: It gave exact facts, the place and time, and a clear fix, moving the boxes to the store room and replacing the toaster.

qa.q: How might Pranav feel receiving this email?
qa.a: Pranav would probably feel thankful and clear about what to do, since the email is calm and specific, which is why the reply says "Good catch".

grounding: Shows a worker reporting a hazard calmly with specific facts and a suggested fix, and the supervisor responding.

passage: When the guard came off the cutting machine for cleaning, the supervisor told me to run one more batch without it. It would save ten minutes. I said no. I did not shout; I said, Hrithik, listen, the guard is off, my hand is close to the blade, and I'm not doing it until it is back on. I offered to run it after the guard was fixed and to stay late to make up the time. My knees were a bit weak. The supervisor stared at me, then sighed and said, fair enough, and called the fitter. The guard was back in twenty minutes, and I finished the batch. It is cheaper to say it early than to explain afterwards. Binita

qa.q: What was off the cutting machine when the supervisor asked for another batch?
qa.a: The guard was off the cutting machine for cleaning.

qa.q: What was Binita feeling when refusing, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Binita felt nervous, since the knees were weak, but stayed calm and specific.

qa.q: What did Binita do that made the refusal easier to accept?
qa.a: Binita gave the facts, offered to run the batch after the guard was back and to stay late, so the refusal came with a fix.

qa.q: How might the supervisor have felt after hearing Binita's refusal?
qa.a: The supervisor probably felt annoyed at first, then accepted the point, and called the fitter, showing the concern was heard.

grounding: Shows a worker refusing an unsafe instruction calmly with specific facts and a suggested fix, and the supervisor's response.
